Hi Lisa — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary of their preference
- Deployment mode: Private VPC (AWS) via PrivateLink is the preferred pattern for Acme Health due to HIPAA requirements.
- Minimum required throughput: ~50 TPS at peak for inference; initial pilot expected 5k/month tokens.
- Data residency: US only.

Open networking / infra questions
1) Will you provision a VPC endpoint (PrivateLink) or are you expecting us to support VPC peering?
2) Which CIDR blocks will you want us to peer with or allow?
3) Any strict egress IP allowlist requirements (static IPs or NAT)?
4) Do you require mutual TLS between Redwood endpoints and your network?

Next steps
- I’ve attached a short network checklist (network-checklist.xlsx) — could you share this with your infra/team and fill the CIDR / firewall details?
- Sean (cc’d) will join a technical deep-dive to map PrivateLink vs peering and cert details. Could you share availability tomorrow or Wednesday morning PST?
- We’ll follow up with a draft SOW and estimated pricing after the technical call.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this into a pilot.

Hi Lisa / Marissa — thanks, appreciate the quick answers. A few technical clarifications ahead of tomorrow’s call so we can prepare: 

PrivateLink vs VPC peering - PrivateLink (AWS PrivateLink / VPC Endpoint Service) is our recommended approach for Acme’s use case — it avoids routing table changes and is compatible with strict CIDR controls. We do support VPC peering for customers that require it, but peering has limitations around overlapping CIDRs and cross-account routing.

Static outbound IPs / Egress - For the control plane (webhooks, callbacks), we can provide a small set of static egress IPs via our NAT gateway pool in the dedicated VPC footprint. For data-plane (inference traffic) most traffic terminates over the PrivateLink endpoint inside your VPC so outbound IP needs are minimal — we can document the set of control-plane IPs you should allow.

mTLS / certs - We support client certificate authentication for management APIs. For the data-plane we can require client certs on request but commonly we use PrivateLink + server-side TLS. If you need strict mTLS, we’ll include the cert exchange steps in the SOW.

Network ports and health checks - We’ll need the following ports open from your side to the interface endpoints: TCP 443 (HTTPS), TCP 9411 (optional tracing), and TCP 8443 (admin control, if proxied). Health checks will be outbound from our control plane on 443 to the endpoint.

Attachment: redwood-vpc-setup-guide.pdf (high level steps, endpoint config snippets).

If you can confirm that 10.20.0.0/16 is correct and whether you can accept our small control-plane IP range (I’ll send the specific addresses in tomorrow’s call prep), we’ll produce a draft SOW with the network appendix and a pilot timeline.

I’ll be on the Tue 10:00 PST slot. Marissa — can you confirm that works for you and Rishi?
